h1: Law of War Training Quiz & Practice Questions
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or point your phone at any Law of War training question for an instant, explained answer — the core principles, explained clearly, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: Law of War Training Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free Law of War training quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Core principles, DoD reporting requirements, and the Law of War Program.
whyItWorks: Law of War questions ask you to apply a small set of core principles — distinction, proportionality, military necessity, humanity — to specific scenarios, and it's easy to mix up which principle governs which situation. Cambo explains the reasoning behind each answer so the principles actually stick.

sampleQuestions.q: Which Law of War principle requires distinguishing between combatants and civilians?
options: Military necessity
Proportionality
Distinction
Humanity
sampleQuestions.a: The principle of distinction — it requires parties to a conflict to distinguish between combatants and civilians, and between military objectives and civilian objects.

sampleQuestions.q: What is a service member required to do if they witness a violation of the Law of War?
options: Report it promptly through the chain of command, as required by DoD Directive 2311.01
Document it privately and raise it only if asked during an investigation
Report it only if the violation resulted in civilian casualties
Take no action unless the violation was committed by a member of their own unit
sampleQuestions.a: Report it through the chain of command — DoD Directive 2311.01 requires all reportable incidents of Law of War violations to be reported promptly.

sampleQuestions.q: Which Law of War principle limits the use of force to what is actually needed to achieve a legitimate military objective?
options: Distinction
Military necessity
Proportionality
Chivalry
sampleQuestions.a: Military necessity — it justifies using force only to the extent required to accomplish a legitimate military purpose, not force for its own sake.

sampleQuestions.q: What does the principle of proportionality prohibit?
options: Any attack that causes incidental harm to civilians under any circumstances
Attacks where expected incidental civilian harm would be excessive relative to the concrete military advantage anticipated
The use of force against a military objective located in a populated area
Any operation carried out without prior warning to the civilian population
sampleQuestions.a: Attacks where the expected incidental harm to civilians or civilian objects would be excessive in relation to the concrete military advantage anticipated.

sampleQuestions.q: Are weapons designed to cause unnecessary suffering permitted under the Law of War?
options: Yes — any weapon is permitted if it is used against a lawful military objective
Yes — provided the weapon is not prohibited by a specific treaty
No — the principle of humanity prohibits weapons or methods that cause suffering beyond what a legitimate military purpose requires
No — but only when the weapon is used against civilians
sampleQuestions.a: No — the principle of humanity prohibits weapons or methods of warfare that cause suffering beyond what's needed to achieve a legitimate military purpose.

sampleQuestions.q: What obligation does the Law of War place on a service member who is ordered to do something they believe is unlawful?
options: They must obey the order and may raise concerns only afterward
They must obey unless a judge advocate is available to consult first
They may disregard any order they personally disagree with
They are not obligated to obey a clearly unlawful order and can be held individually responsible for war crimes committed under one
sampleQuestions.a: Service members are not obligated to obey a clearly unlawful order and can be held individually responsible for war crimes committed under one — "just following orders" isn't a blanket defense.

faqs.q: How often is Law of War training required?
faqs.a: Requirements vary by service branch and role, but it's generally required at initial entry training and refreshed periodically throughout a service member's career.

faqs.q: Who has to complete Law of War training?
faqs.a: All members of the U.S. armed forces, with more in-depth training for commanders, legal practitioners, and personnel in operational roles.

faqs.q: What are the core Law of War principles?
faqs.a: Military necessity, distinction, proportionality, and humanity (avoiding unnecessary suffering) — these four principles underlie most Law of War rules and analysis.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense.

faqs.q: What is the DoD Law of War Manual?
faqs.a: A comprehensive DoD-wide resource developed by military and civilian lawyers to guide commanders, legal practitioners, and personnel on the law of war and how it applies to military operations.

faqs.q: Does Law of War training apply during all operations, or just declared wars?
faqs.a: It applies broadly — the Law of War Program requires compliance with the law of war during all armed conflicts, however characterized, and DoD policy directs adherence even in operations other than war.
